code_semantics.chosen_plan_death_frame_is: Plan.death_frame — the geometry/hazard-tape model prediction copied by _replace, not VerifiedPlan.death_frame read from the engine

findings.statement: 20 decisions have bomb=1 while their frame_event_flags carries no PLAYER_HIT bit. decide.py sets bomb=1 in exactly two branches: bomb rule 1, gated by 'all_verified_die = bool(verified) and not survivors', and the death bomb, gated by player_hit, which is bit 0x2 of that same EVENTS word. With the bit absent only rule 1 can have fired, so in these decisions every verified plan — here the single verified plan — was killed by the engine. All of them still carry verified_mask=True, chosen_plan.verified=True and chosen_plan.death_frame=null, so the row is indistinguishable from a survived decision. This is the positive proof that verified_mask=True is not survival.

verified_mask[cand]=True means only 'verify_plans returned a plan whose first_action is cand'. decide.py sets it True for every returned verified plan without consulting died, and when every verified plan dies the chosen plan is still re-marked verified=True. Survivorship is decided by VerifiedPlan.died, which this row schema does not carry, so verified_mask=True cannot be read as 'survived'.

The D1 row written by ObsShardWriter._label_row stores chosen_plan only, and chosen_plan is search.Plan, which has no died / frames_advanced / trajectory_matches / verification_horizon. Those fields exist on VerifiedPlan in verify.py but are dropped by the writer, so no surviving or dying plan can be re-checked from D1 labels — and the missing fields are recorded as absent, not as a pass.

0 of 34013 decisions have chosen_plan.verified=True together with a non-null chosen_plan.death_frame. That frame is Plan.death_frame, the geometry model's prediction copied by _replace — not the engine's VerifiedPlan.death_frame — so a non-null value would mean 'a verified plan the geometry model expects to die', not an engine-confirmed death. This sample contains 0 such row(s), so the 'verified but dead' case is not demonstrated by that field here; it is demonstrated instead by the 20 bomb=1 rows without PLAYER_HIT, whose chosen_plan.death_frame is null — the geometry model predicted survival where the engine killed the plan.

scores are stored post-discount: the verified candidate keeps its raw score while every other finite candidate is lowered by unverified_discount=5.0. With one verified candidate per row the top1-top2 gap is therefore discount + true geometric gap, and argmax(scores) is the verified candidate by construction. The gap cannot be used as a teacher confidence measure, and 'top1 = chosen action' is not evidence of a geometric preference.

verified_count is ['1'] in every sampled row: only one of the 18 first actions is ever engine-verified (the collector ran mode=fast, verify_k=1). verified_mask=False is therefore 'not verified', never 'unsafe', and 17/18 of every row's action space has no engine evidence at all.

29946 of 34013 rows report margin == 16.0 (MARGIN_CAP): the margin term is capped, so those rows say 'at least 16 px of clearance' and cannot separate near misses. A low-margin diagnostic set (WP02 item 4) can only be selected from the rows below the cap.

frames_per_decision=4 and decision_frames=2 are different quantities: frames_per_decision = replan_decisions x decision_frames = 2 x 2. The pair is unequal in 34013/34013 rows while the product relation holds in 34013/34013 rows, so flagging 4 != 2 as a data defect would be a false positive. What is auditable is the relation itself, the decision_frame stride and the obs.label_frames length.

findings.statement: Two shards of the same stage but different seeds share byte-identical label content for their first 1298 sampled decisions before diverging. Shard count is therefore not independent-label count: any 'N independent trajectories' claim (WP02 item 4, WP03 coverage) has to deduplicate by label content, not by shard directory.

The row-level 'stage' (and 'difficulty') written into every label is constant ['0'] even in shards whose shard.json says stage 1/3/6/7 and difficulty 1. Per-stage or per-difficulty stratification cannot be done from labels.jsonl: this audit groups by shard.json stage/difficulty and records the row field separately. Downstream code that buckets samples by record['stage'] collapses every stage into one.
Integrity counters raised by the row decoder; a non-zero count means the row schema and the code disagree (see the per-shard blocks).

not_claimed: Not a G410-1 teacher gate result: this audit reads labels only and never measures the teacher's clear rate on confirmed seeds.
Not a capability conclusion: no student, no policy evaluation, no training, no game launch, no data collection.
Not a full-corpus audit: 10 shard(s) with at most 5000 rows each were read; the D1 tree has more shards and this sample does not stand in for them.
Missing fields are not a pass: died / frames_advanced / trajectory_matches / verification_horizon never appearing in D1 rows is recorded as absent and blocks any survival claim, not satisfied.
chosen_plan.death_frame is not an engine death: it is the geometry model's prediction copied by decide._replace, and the sampled corpus contains no non-null instance.

bomb=1 rows without PLAYER_HIT are *inferred* to be engine-confirmed deaths of a verified plan from the decide.py rule-1 path plus the absent bit; the row itself still has no died field, so the inference is only as strong as the code reading recorded in code_semantics (claims code.11-code.14).
verified_mask=False is not 'unsafe': unverified candidates are unlabelled for safety, not negative examples.
Identical label streams across seeds do not prove identical engine states: hash_pre/hash_post differ by seed and are excluded from the fingerprint.
No engine, no third_party/, no v380/v390/v400 source was modified; no D1 file was written, moved or deleted.
